data.long_meaning: Mayur is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Mayura' which means peacock. In Hindu mythology, the peacock is considered a sacred bird, symbolizing wealth, prosperity, and the grace of the gods. The name Mayur is believed to bring good fortune and joy. The name Mayur carries the meaning “Peacock” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mayur usually hope their child will grow to embody peacock and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Peacock feathers have been used in royal headdresses, decorations, and fan motifs for centuries in Indian art and culture. The peacock is also the national bird of India and is seen as a symbol of power and status.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the peacock is one of the Vahanas (vehicles) of Lord Mahadeva, the God of Destruction. It is also associated with Lord Murugan or Kartikeya, the God of War and Victory, and Lord Indra, the God of Rain and Thunder. The peacock's beautiful plumage is said to represent the power of transformation and the attainment of spiritual enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mayur symbolizes joy, beauty, and grace, as it is the name of the peacock in Hinduism, adorned with a thousand eyes, representing wisdom and the all-seeing aspect of the divine.

vedic_reference.note: The name of the peacock, the vehicle of Lord Indra, and also of Lord Murugan in Tamil and Lord Ganesha in Maharashtra.

historical_references.reference: Mayur was the name of a legendary king in ancient India, who ruled over the Vidarbha region in Maharashtra. He is remembered for his valor and justice in Indian folklore.
historical_references.context: Mayur is a popular character in Indian mythology and literature, and his tales are often narrated in various forms of Indian art and storytelling.

historical_references.reference: Mayur is also the name of a legendary bird in Hindu mythology, symbolizing happiness, prosperity, and good fortune. It is depicted with feathers like peacock, and its flesh is believed to be delicious and nourishing.
historical_references.context: Mayur is often invoked in Hindu rituals and ceremonies to bring about happiness, good luck, and prosperity.
